topPRs.title: feat: add `SetReviewPeriodDelays` template for the per-chain withdrawal delays
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
## Summary

One `L2TaskBase` template, `SetReviewPeriodDelays`, for the per-chain withdrawal delay setters from ethereum-optimism/optimism#23215 and ethereum-optimism/optimism#23252. It sets `OptimismPortal2.proofMaturityDelaySeconds`, `AnchorStateRegistry.disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds` and `DelayedWETH.delay` for every chain in the task in one Safe transaction, so an operator signs once for the whole set.

Draft until the setters are deployed on a Sepolia chain the registry can address.

## Context

The monorepo PRs move the three delays from implementation immutables to per-chain proxy storage with ProxyAdminOwner-only setters bounded by min/max. No template can call them today. After interop migration the ASR and the DelayedWETH are shared by a set while proof maturity stays per portal, so the template is scoped to a whole set and asserts uniform proof maturity across portals sharing an ETHLockbox.

## Changes

- `src/template/SetReviewPeriodDelays.sol`: every `[delays]` key optional, one value for all chains; bounds check against each contract's min/max at setup; a setter is only called where the on-chain value differs, and a shared ASR or DelayedWETH is written once, so the batch holds exactly the calls for the configured keys (one portal call per chain, one call per shared contract); DelayedWETH resolved from `SystemConfig.delayedWETH()` and registered for the storage allow-list; `_validate` asserts each value per chain, then the per-lockbox uniformity check (isolated in `_checkSetUniformity`).
- `test/template/SetReviewPeriodDelaysToml.t.sol`: no-fork tests for the parser and bounds check.
- `test/tasks/example/sep/044-set-review-period-delays`: example task on sepolia-devnet-2 and -3.
- `test/tasks/Regression.t.sol`: one case, fixture pending.

Interfaces are declared inline, as the template boilerplate requires.

## Notes

- Setters are not deployed anywhere yet: the example task reverts at `minProofMaturityDelaySeconds()`, so `template_regression_tests` and the regression case fail. After deployment: re-pin the block in `.env` and the test, capture call data and data to sign into the regression case, run `just simulate-all-templates`, un-draft.
- The uniformity check only sees the chains in the task (set membership is not enumerable on-chain), and the policy itself is not confirmed. Dropping it is deleting `_checkSetUniformity`.
- Confirm the `Supports:` versions against the release tag.

Closes [#697](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/697)

topPRs.title: [CONTINGENCY] sep/119: Soneium Minato rollback of batcher + unsafe block signer
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
Contingency rollback for the Soneium Minato sequencer + batcher cutover in #1565, the Sepolia twin of the mainnet rollback in #1588. Kept as a separate PR and merged only if it is needed.

`sep/119` restores Sony's batcher `0xF0AB0441c8f4B89b561aE685B98c6aD5175e0CAB` and unsafe block signer `0x55930859CD7003F32A2ba171297408476532E535` (the live values before `sep/117`) on the Minato `SystemConfigProxy`, signed by the Sepolia FoundationUpgradeSafe, which stays the SystemConfig owner. The proposer (`sep/116`) has no rollback.

It is pinned to FoundationUpgradeSafe nonce 84, shared with the foundation approval of `sep/118` (fee vaults), so only one of the two can execute: `sep/118` is executed only once the cutover is confirmed, and if the rollback executes instead, `sep/118` moves up by one nonce and is re-signed. The status `CANCELLED (CONTINGENCY TASK, SIGN AS NEEDED)` keeps it out of the stacked simulation. It is simulated on its own, with state overrides for the post-`sep/117` owner, batcher and signer.

The calldata is `sep/117`'s with Sony's two addresses swapped in, checked byte for byte and decoded with `cast`. The standalone simulation passes, and the hashes in VALIDATION.md come from it.

topPRs.title: [CONTINGENCY] eth/088: Soneium Mainnet rollback of batcher + unsafe block signer
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
Contingency rollback for the Soneium Mainnet sequencer + batcher cutover in #1566. Kept as a separate PR and merged only if it is needed, same as the Ink rollback in #1493.

`eth/088` restores Sony's batcher `0x6776BE80dBAda6A02B5F2095cF13734ac303B8d1` and unsafe block signer `0x7c2Bd59ee2a2C7391c9A240132f26071e9546262` (the live values before `eth/085`) on the Soneium `SystemConfigProxy`, signed by the FoundationUpgradeSafe, which stays the SystemConfig owner. The proposer has no rollback: the OPE proposer (`eth/084`) keeps working whichever party runs the sequencer and batcher.

It is pinned to FoundationUpgradeSafe nonce 82, so it can be signed ahead of the Nov 19 ceremony and executed within minutes. That nonce is shared with the foundation approval of `eth/086` (fee vaults), so only one of the two can execute. `eth/086` should be executed only once the cutover is confirmed. If the rollback executes instead, `eth/086` and every later FUS task (`eth/087`) move up by one nonce and are re-signed. The status is `CANCELLED (CONTINGENCY TASK, SIGN AS NEEDED)` so `fetch-tasks.sh` leaves it out of the stacked simulation, where the shared nonce would otherwise fail the nonce check. It is simulated on its own, with state overrides for the post-`eth/085` owner, batcher and signer.

The calldata is `eth/085`'s with Sony's two addresses swapped in, checked byte for byte and decoded with `cast`. The standalone simulation passes, and the hashes in VALIDATION.md come from it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: fix(template): fork L2 pre-flight 5 blocks behind the reported head
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
Fixes the intermittent `stacked_simulation_eth` failures on main since #1564 ([CI alert thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C03N11M0BBN/p1792153643217549)).

**Cause** `SetL1SplitterConfig` (eth/076, eth/079) and `SetFeeVaultConfig` (eth/080) dry-run on an L2 fork of `https://mainnet.unichain.org` taken at `latest`. That endpoint is load-balanced: one backend reports a head that the backend serving the next request does not have yet, so the fork reads empty state. 

**Fix** Both templates fork `L2_FORK_HEAD_LAG = 5` blocks behind `eth_blockNumber`. The pre-flight still sees live state, about 5s old. Pinned regression harnesses override `_createL2Fork` and are unaffected. Signed calldata and hashes don't change.

**Verification** `just simulate-stack eth` passes locally for eth/074–080, and every domain/message hash matches its VALIDATION.md.
